result:
None of the three solutions has the correct final answer.

The clearest check is the case j = k+1, i.e. only one unshaded rectangle U. Every shaded rectangle must share an edge with U, since the shaded rectangles are pairwise non-adjacent and the polygon is connected. Each shaded rectangle contributes two convex far corners, and U's corners can only add convex corners or reflex corners at its contact points. Applying c − r = 4 to the polygon gives r ≥ 2k − 4, so the polygon has at least 4 + 2(2k−4) = 4k − 4 sides. For example, S(11,10) ≥ 36.

Solution 1 uses S(11,10) = 22, Solution 2 uses 6, and Solution 3 uses 28. All three fall below this lower bound, so their totals cannot be right.

I could not pin down the exact value of the full sum, because the cases with more than one unshaded rectangle depend on more delicate configurations.

CHOICE: NONE
